tb-204-1.question:
The magnitude of the resultant of a 3-N force and a 4-N force cannot be

A 0 N.

B 1 N.

C 4 N.

D 7 N.
tb-204-1.reasoning: The magnitude of the resultant force of a 3-N force and a 4-N force cannot be smaller than 1 N.

tb-204-2.question: A signboard is hung by two identical wires. Which of the following is the safest way to hang it?
tb-204-2.reasoning:
In option A, the tension in each wire is equal to half the weight of the signboard.

In options B and D, the tensions in the wires are larger than those in A since there are horizontal components contributing to their magnitudes.

In options C, only one wire, which is inclined, is providing upward force to the signboard. So, the tension in that wire is larger than the weight of the signboard.

tb-204-3.question:
Blocks X, Y and Z are put together on a smooth horizontal plane and a horizontal force F acts on X (Fig a).

Which of the following statements is/are correct?

(1) The force acting on Z by Y is equal to F.

(2) The force acting on Z by Y has the same magnitude as the force acting on X by Y.

(3) The force acting on Y by X has the same magnitude as the force acting on X by Y.

A (2) only

B (3) only

C (1) and (2) only

D (1) and (3) only
tb-204-3.reasoning:
The three blocks will move together as a whole. Their acceleration will be FmX+mY+mZ.

(1): If the force acting on Z by Y equals F,
the acceleration of Z =FmZ>FmX+mY+mZ. Since there is a contradiction, (1) is incorrect.

(3): The force acting on Y by X and the force acting on X by Y is an action-and-reaction pair. (3) is correct.

(2): The force acting on Y by X must be larger than that acting on Y by Z to make Y accelerate towards the right. By Newton’s third law of motion, the force acting on X by Y must be larger than that acting on Z by Y. (2) is incorrect.

tb-204-4.question:
A box is placed on the floor of a container truck such that it is up against the wall of the container (Fig b). The truck is moving towards the right at a constant velocity.

Which of the following is the correct free-body diagram for the box?
tb-204-4.reasoning:
The truck and box move at constant velocity, so the box has zero acceleration. Its downward weight and the upward normal force from the floor balance.

Merely being against the wall does not imply a horizontal force: there is no horizontal acceleration pressing the box into it. No frictional force is needed to maintain uniform motion. Diagram A is correct.

tb-204-5.question:
A kangaroo of mass 80 kg lands on the ground (Fig c). At this moment, the force acting on it by the ground is 960 N. This force makes an angle of 75° to the horizontal. Find the magnitude of the net force acting on it.

A 175 N

B 286 N

C 1070 N

D 1730 N
tb-204-5.reasoning:
Horizontal component of net force

= 960 cos 75°

= 248.5 N

Vertical component of net force

= 960 sin 75° – mg

= 960 sin 75° – (80)(9.81)

= 142.5 N

Magnitude of net force

=248.52+142.52

= 286 N

tb-204-11.question:
Block X of mass 2 kg is placed on a rough inclined plane while block Y of mass 0.5 kg is placed on block X (Fig h). Both blocks are stationary. The rough plane is at an angle of 15° to the horizontal.

B 19.6 N

C 23.7 N

tb-204-12.question:
A man of mass 70 kg sits in a train that accelerates constantly at 0.8 m s−2 up a rail inclined at 15° (Fig i). What is the magnitude of the force acting on the man by the train?

A 216 N

B 687 N

C 703 N

D 743 N
tb-204-12.reasoning:
Fnet = ma

= (70)(0.8)

= 56 N

The net force is 56 N (up the rail).

Let Fx and Fy be the horizontal and vertical components of the force acting on the man by the train.

Consider the horizontal direction.

Fx = Fnet cos 15°

= (56) cos 15°

= 54.1 N

Consider the vertical direction.

Fy− mg = Fnet sin 15°

Fy − (70)(9.81) = (56) sin 15°

Fy = 701 N

Magnitude of the force acting on the man by the train

=54.12+7012

= 703 N

tb-204-13.question:
Blocks X and Y are placed on a smooth plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. A horizontal force of 50 N acts on X (Fig j). The weight of X is 20 N and the weight of Y is 30 N. Find the magnitude of the force acting on X by Y.

A 0

B 7.32 N

C 26.0 N

D 36.6 N
tb-204-13.reasoning:
Consider the system of X and Y.

Consider the direction parallel to the plane.

Take the direction up the plane as positive.

Fnet = 50 cos 30° – (20 + 30) sin 30°

= 18.3 N

By Fnet = ma,

18.3 =(2030)9.81a

a = 3.59 m s−2

Consider X.

Let F be the force acting on X by Y.

By Fnet = ma,

50 cos 30° – F – 20 sin 30° =209.81(3.59)

F = 26.0 N

tb-204-14.question:
A spring gun of mass 1 kg projects a ball of mass 0.2 kg vertically upwards. At a certain instant, the acceleration of the ball is 5 m s−2 upwards (Fig k). What is the normal force acting on the spring gun by the floor at this instant?

A 9.81 N

B 10.8 N

C 11.8 N

D 12.8 N
tb-204-14.reasoning:
Let F be the force acting on the ball by the gun at that moment.

Consider the ball.

By Fnet = ma,

F – mg = ma

F – (0.2)(9.81) = (0.2)(5)

F = 2.96 N

By Newton’s third law of motion, the ball exerts a downward force with the same magnitude F on the spring gun.

Normal force acting on the spring gun by the floor

= F + mg = 2.96 + (1)(9.81) = 12.8 N

At t = 5 s,

a =8−010−0 1M

= 0.8 m s−2 (up the slope) 1A

(b) Consider the motion of A in the direction along the slope.

By Fnet = ma,

T – f – mg sin 20° = ma

T – 10 000 – (20 000)(9.81) sin 20°

= (20 000)(0.8) 1M

T = 93 100 N 1A

The tension is 93 100 N.

(c) Consider the motion of B in the direction along the slope.

A and B move at the same speed in opposite direction.

∴ a = –0.8 m s−2

By Fnet = ma,

T + f – mg sin 20° = ma

T + 10 000 – (20 000)(9.81) sin 20°

= (20 000)(–0.8) 1M

T = 41 100 N 1A

The tension is 41 100 N.

(d) Consider the motion of A.
